title: Add scheduled cost-model drift monitoring job (predicted vs observed) + exported metrics
author: Thomas Baird
description:
Context: As we roll Console + Optimize onto the Standard Cost Model primitives, we need an automated signal that predicted/request-attributed costs remain consistent with observed spend allocation over a reporting window. This PR adds a scheduled drift monitoring job that (1) aggregates predicted cost outputs from the Cost Model pipeline (prefill/decode split + overhead allocation) and (2) compares them against observed costs (GPU spend allocation + billing primitives) over the same window, then (3) exports bounded-cardinality metrics for dashboards/alerts.

What this adds: (a) A Kubernetes CronJob (hourly) that computes drift for a configured set of dimensions (deployment_mode, sku_family, region, model_id, quant_profile_id) with hard caps to avoid cardinality blowups. (b) A canonical drift calculation (ratio + absolute delta) with explicit handling for telemetry lag and partial windows. (c) Prometheus metrics exported via the existing internal metrics gateway so Grafana dashboards/alerts can be built on top (tracked in observability-pack PR).

Key metrics emitted (names are stable; labels are bounded): cost_model_drift_ratio{window="1h|24h",deployment_mode,region,sku_family,model_id,quant_profile_id}; cost_model_drift_usd_abs{window=...,same_labels}; cost_model_predicted_usd_total{window=...}; cost_model_observed_usd_total{window=...}; cost_model_drift_samples_total{window=...}; cost_model_telemetry_lag_seconds{source="token_metering|gpu_spend"}; cost_model_drift_job_success (gauge) + cost_model_drift_job_duration_seconds (histogram).

Drift calculation details: drift_ratio = (predicted_usd_total - observed_usd_total) / max(observed_usd_total, epsilon_usd). Epsilon defaults to $5 for 1h windows to avoid noisy division on tiny totals; 24h uses $50. We also export abs delta so alerting can key off either ratio or dollars. Windows supported: 1h rolling (for fast regressions) and 24h rolling (for finance alignment). The job refuses to compute drift if telemetry lag exceeds configured thresholds (default: token metering > 20m lag OR gpu spend allocation > 2h lag), and emits a lag metric + sets drift metrics to "stale" via a separate gauge so dashboards can annotate.

Data sources: Predicted costs are pulled from the cost-model aggregation table (the same one Console uses for breakdown views) at schema_version >= v1. Observed costs are pulled from the daily GPU spend allocation feed joined to Redwood internal deployment inventory; for hosted, we use the standardized billing primitives table (request-attributed) as the observed baseline until the GPU allocation feed is fully attributable at request-level.

Bounds & performance: Job enforces top-N selection by total predicted_usd_total per window (default top 200 label combinations) plus an allowlist for high-revenue tenants in prod. Dimensions are configured in a YAML so we can reduce label set without code changes. Query plans were validated against staging with 7d data; p95 job runtime 42s on staging; prod budget is < 3m.

Failure modes: If either data source is unavailable, job exits non-zero and emits failure count; if only a subset of dimensions can be computed, we emit metrics for computed dims but also emit a "partial" gauge. The CronJob is protected by a feature flag (COST_MODEL_DRIFT_JOB_ENABLED) and ships disabled by default in non-prod until SRE signs off.

Why now: We had a recent support escalation (SUP-31844) where Console cost breakdown diverged from invoice totals; drift monitoring should surface this class of regression (schema mismatch, telemetry lag, prefill/decode accounting bug, overhead allocation changes) earlier and provide an objective SLI input for ENG-4827.

Testing: Unit tests cover drift math, epsilon behavior, lag gating, top-N selection, and label bounding. Integration test runs the job against a fixture dataset (predicted + observed) and asserts exported metric series count stays under bound. Added a dry-run mode that logs computed drift rows without exporting metrics for staging validation.

Rollout plan: (1) Merge + deploy job disabled. (2) Enable in staging for 1 week; validate against manual finance reconciliation. (3) Enable in prod for 1h window only; run for 48h. (4) Enable 24h window + alert thresholds after we have stable baseline. Alert configuration and dashboards are in follow-up PRs; SRE owns alert tuning.

review_conversation: Logan Wright: Can we make telemetry lag gating explicit and observable? We’ve seen false positives when token metering is delayed. Also please confirm we’re not joining on high-cardinality request ids anywhere.

Thomas Baird (author): Added cost_model_telemetry_lag_seconds{source=...} and a lag gate (token metering 20m, spend allocation 2h). No request-id joins; predicted side is aggregated table keyed by model/deployment dims.

Nadia Rahman: Prefill/decode accounting—are we aggregating predicted totals as (prefill + decode + overhead) or just request-attributable? We need to match the observed baseline and make semantics obvious.

Thomas Baird (author): Predicted uses total_usd including overhead_usd (per ADR-022), but we also emit predicted_usd_total and expose drift against observed_usd_total. Added README section clarifying that for hosted observed baseline is billing primitives (request-attributed) until gpu allocation feed is request-attributable; config allows switching observed source per deployment_mode.

Rafael Mendes: CronJob needs safe bounds. Top-N should be deterministic and stable window-to-window, and we should cap series emitted. Also add a kill-switch + make sure failure increments are alerted on separately.

Thomas Baird (author): Implemented top-N by predicted_usd_total desc with stable tie-break (model_id then quant_profile_id). Hard cap 200 series/window plus allowlist. Added COST_MODEL_DRIFT_JOB_ENABLED flag and cost_model_drift_job_success gauge + duration histogram.
Allison Grant: Metric naming: please avoid embedding too much semantics into labels, and ensure window is a label not in the name. Also confirm histogram buckets are standard.
Thomas Baird (author): Updated names to cost_model_drift_ratio and cost_model_drift_usd_abs with window label. Histogram uses standard job duration buckets from our observability library.

Cole Summers: This references SUP-31844; can you add a note that this is not a billing system of record and drift alerts should not page Finance directly? Also please document how we handle overhead policy updates.

Thomas Baird (author): Added docs note: for billing/RevRec this is an engineering correctness signal only; alerts route to cost-model oncall (SRE + platform). Overhead policy changes should be accompanied by a baseline reset/annotation; added config knob for suppressing alerts during scheduled policy migrations.
Rafael Mendes: Approve with request: keep prod default disabled and require explicit enable via flag in release config.
Thomas Baird (author): Done; manifests ship disabled, and flag is false by default across envs.
Approvals: Logan Wright (approved), Nadia Rahman (approved), Rafael Mendes (approved), Allison Grant (approved), Cole Summers (approved)
release_notes: Internal-only: adds cost-model drift monitoring CronJob + exported metrics (disabled by default). Enables dashboards/alerts for predicted vs observed cost drift (ENG-4827).
